evidence.intree_statement: Proposition UniversalArrowIsUniversalProperty : IsUniversalProperty D (fun a : D => AUniversalArrow c U a) _.  (* proof term, Defined, fixes repr_functor := (Curried_Hom C c) ◯ U, i.e. d ↦ Hom_C(c, U d); so AUniversalArrow c U a ≅ { natural isos [Hom a,─] ≅ Hom_C(c, U ─) } as setoids — the representability half of the criterion, in both directions *)

Class UniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) := { arrow_initial : @Initial (=(c) ↓ F); arrow_obj := snd (`1 (@initial_obj _ arrow_initial)); arrow : c ~> F arrow_obj := `2 (@initial_obj _ arrow_initial) }.  (* the universal property IS initiality of the comma category =(c) ↓ F *)

Definition universal_arrow_from_UMP (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) (d : D) (η : c ~> fobj[F] d) (u : ∀ (d' : D) (f : c ~> fobj[F] d'), ∃! g : d ~> d', f ≈ fmap[F] g ∘ η) : UniversalArrow c F.  (* converse: the universal mapping property reconstructs the initial object of the comma category; with ump_universal_arrows (:139) this makes the correspondence a biconditional *)

statement_record.book: By duality, a CONTRAVARIANT functor F : C^op ⟶ Set is representable if and only if its category of elements ∫F has a TERMINAL object; the exercise asks to obtain this by dualizing the covariant proof (Proposition 2.4.8, representable ⟺ ∫F has an initial object).
statement_record.intree: Class UniversalArrow (c : C) (F : D ⟶ C) := { arrow_initial : @Initial (=(c) ↓ F); ... } together with Proposition UniversalArrowIsUniversalProperty : IsUniversalProperty D (fun a : D => AUniversalArrow c U a) _ (repr_functor = d ↦ Hom_C(c, U d)) and Definition universal_arrow_from_UMP ... : UniversalArrow c F.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: three ways. (1) The category of elements ∫F is not in the library at all; the stand-in is the comma category =(c) ↓ F, which is never identified with ∫F. (2) The functor whose representability is characterized is not an arbitrary Sets-valued functor but one of the shape Hom_C(c, U ─); recovering an arbitrary F : C ⟶ Sets needs Hom_Sets(1, F ─) ≅ F, which is NOT proven in-tree (searched Instance/Sets.v and Structure/Constant.v — only Sets_Terminal and the 'global element' vocabulary exist). (3) The orientation is the covariant/INITIAL one; the terminal/contravariant form the exercise actually asks for appears in-tree only as a prose remark (Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:23-24, 'The dual notion, a universal arrow from F to c, is a terminal object of F ↓ =(c)'), which is a comment, not an assertion. It is obtainable by instantiating the above at opposite categories (the library's standard duality idiom), but no file does so.

gap: The contravariant/terminal statement itself is nowhere asserted — it exists only as a prose remark at Theory/Universal/Arrow.v:23-24. What IS proven is the covariant/initial correspondence 'a represents Hom_C(c, U ─) ⟺ (a, u) is an initial object of the comma =(c) ↓ U'. To close the gap one needs: the category of elements ∫F as a construction; its identification with =(1) ↓ F (via Hom_Sets(1, X) ≅ X, also missing); and the dualized statement 'F : C^op ⟶ Sets representable ⟺ ∫F has a terminal object' as an actual in-tree theorem.

evidence.intree_statement: Proposition CartesianProductIsUniversalProperty : IsUniversalProperty C^op (fun z => IsCartesianProduct x y z) (fun z => CartesianProductStructuresEquiv x y z).  (* proof is Defined and fixes repr_functor := [Hom ─ , x ] × [Hom ─ , y ]; unfolding IsUniversalProperty, for each z the setoid of witnesses 'z is a product of x and y' is isomorphic in Sets to the setoid of natural isos [Hom z,─] ≅ [Hom ─,x] × [Hom ─,y]. Instantiated at C := C^op (the library's own idiom, since Notation Cocartesian C := @Cartesian (C^op) and C^op^op = C by reflexivity) this reads: z is a COPRODUCT of x and y in C iff Hom_C(z,─) ≅ Hom_C(x,─) × Hom_C(y,─) — i.e. C(x,─) × C(y,─) is representable exactly by x + y *)

Class IsCartesianProduct (x y z : C) := { fork' {a} (f : a ~> x) (g : a ~> y) : a ~> z; exl' : z ~> x; exr' : z ~> y; fork'_respects : ∀ a, Proper (equiv ==> equiv ==> equiv) (@fork' a); ump_product {a} (f : a ~> x) (g : a ~> y) (h : a ~> z) : h ≈ fork' f g ↔ (exl' ∘ h ≈ f) * (exr' ∘ h ≈ g) }.  (* the predicate the proposition above characterizes; read in C^op its data is inl : x ~> z, inr : y ~> z and the copairing, and ump_product becomes h ≈ f ▽ g ↔ (h ∘ inl ≈ f) * (h ∘ inr ≈ g) — the elementwise form of the bijection Hom(x + y, a) ≅ Hom(x, a) × Hom(y, a) *)

statement_record.book: For fixed objects A, B of a locally small category C, consider C(A,─) × C(B,─) : C ⟶ Set, X ↦ C(A,X) × C(B,X). What would it mean for this functor to be representable? (Answer: a representing object is precisely a coproduct A ⊔ B, its universal element the pair of coproduct injections.)
statement_record.intree: Proposition CartesianProductIsUniversalProperty : IsUniversalProperty C^op (fun z => IsCartesianProduct x y z) (fun z => CartesianProductStructuresEquiv x y z), with repr_functor = [Hom ─ , x ] × [Hom ─ , y ] and IsUniversalProperty C P eqP := { repr_functor : C ⟶ Sets; repr_equivalence : ∀ c, P c ≅ (Isomorphism [Hom c,─] repr_functor) in Sets }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, with two presentational caveats. (a) The theorem is stated for PRODUCTS and delivers the exercise's coproduct/covariant reading by instantiating its universally quantified C at C^op — legitimate and free here, because the library defines coproducts exactly that way (Notation Cocartesian C := @Cartesian (C^op), Structure/Cocartesian.v:115) and C^op^op = C holds by reflexivity; but no in-tree file spells out the coproduct-named corollary, so the reader must perform the instantiation. (b) The representing functor [Hom ─,x] × [Hom ─,y] appears in the (transparent, Defined) proof term rather than in the type; the type alone asserts only that SOME representing functor makes the equivalence hold. The pointwise product of Sets-valued functors the exercise needs is the in-tree × of Instance/Fun/Cartesian.v, exactly the one used here. Strength is otherwise identical: an isomorphism of setoids in both directions, not merely one implication.

CONFIRMED PRESENT — and I upgraded the confirmation from reading to MACHINE CHECKING, because the record's claim rests on an instantiation no in-tree file performs.   Check (fun C : Category => eq_refl : (C^op)^op = C).                          (* accepted *)
  Definition CoproductIsUniversalProperty (C : Category) (x y : C) :
    IsUniversalProperty C (fun z => @IsCartesianProduct (C^op) x y z)
                          (fun z => @CartesianProductStructuresEquiv (C^op) x y z)
    := CartesianProductIsUniversalProperty (C^op) x y.                          (* typechecks *)
  Goal forall (C : Category) (x y z : C),
    Sets.carrier (repr_functor (CoproductIsUniversalProperty C x y) z)
      = ((x ~{C}~> z) * (y ~{C}~> z))%type.  Proof. reflexivity. Qed.           (* closes *)
So the instantiation at C^op is free (C^op^op = C by eq_refl, as the library's duality architecture promises), it yields a statement ABOUT C, and its representing functor computes DEFINITIONALLY to z ↦ C(x,z) × C(y,z) — exactly the functor of the exercise, with @IsCartesianProduct (C^op) x y z being the library's own reading of 'z is a coproduct of x and y' (Notation Cocartesian C := @Cartesian (C^op)).
